description: Visual and interaction quality gate for Horizon Church V2 frontend work.

scoring.hard_fail: Any failed hard_fail rule blocks completion regardless of score.
scoring.score_formula: Sum weights for passed scored rules / total applicable scored-rule weight * 100.
scoring.not_applicable: Rules outside the changed surface may be marked N/A and excluded from the denominator.

hard_fail_rules.rule: No arbitrary chromatic accent color is introduced for routine UI emphasis.
Short create/edit CRUD forms use an accessible modal/dialog rather than rendering inline above/below the management list unless explicitly approved.
Every modal/drawer is keyboard operable, Escape-closeable when safe, focus-trapped, and restores focus to its trigger.
The page has no document-level horizontal overflow at 390px viewport width.
All interactive controls have visible keyboard focus and icon-only controls have accessible names.
No business behavior, authorization rule, or locked product decision is changed merely to satisfy the visual system.
No secret/private backend credential is exposed to browser code while implementing UI/theme work.
Reduced-motion preferences are respected for nonessential animation.

checks.rule: Routine interface is monochrome and uses semantic background/ink/gray tokens.
Primary action uses inversion rather than accent color.
Status meaning is conveyed by text/iconography and not color alone.
Geist or approved UI fallback is used consistently for body/UI typography.
Mono micro-label treatment is used selectively for metadata, section markers, table headers, or statuses.
Display/pixel typography is restrained and not used for ordinary body/form/table text.
Whitespace and alignment provide structure; the screen is not dominated by nested cards.
Management content uses an appropriate wide measure rather than a narrow reading column.
Page header has clear hierarchy and primary action placement.
Active sidebar item uses ink/marker/weight rather than a large tinted rectangle.
Sidebar groups/user area use hairlines or spacing rather than heavy cards.
Borders are predominantly one-pixel hairlines using semantic gray tokens.
Radius usage follows a coherent 16/12/8/6-style ladder.
Shadows are soft and restrained; dark mode relies more on borders.
Primary, secondary, ghost, and destructive actions have clear hierarchy without decorative gradients.
Inputs have minimal borders/fills, readable labels, concise helper/error copy, and visible focus.
Modal uses restrained dim/blur overlay, centered soft-radius panel, and compact actions.
Management tables use hairline row separation, compact headers, readable primary/secondary text, and restrained hover.
Secondary row actions use an ellipsis/action menu when this reduces button clutter.
Empty state is concise and does not default to a huge bordered box.
Halftone texture is used sparingly and never as dense-content wallpaper.
Light/dark/system behavior uses semantic token remapping.
Explicit theme choice persists and defaults to system.
Motion is brief, eased, non-bouncy, and subordinate to usability.
Semantic landmarks, form labels, dialog labelling, contrast, and keyboard navigation are preserved.
Desktop, tablet transition, and 390px mobile remain legible and usable.
Login stays calm and monochrome, with halftone/typography carrying brand character.
The result feels like a practical church operations product, not a portfolio mockup or generic SaaS dashboard.

scenario_evals.prompt: Restyle the Horizon Life Groups management page and convert create/edit to the Horizon Minimal interaction system.
expected: black/inverted New Life Group primary action
no inline form pushing list downward

scenario_evals.prompt: Build a Members management list and create-member flow using Horizon Minimal.
expected: Life Group visible in create form
create form in modal unless complexity justifies dedicated page

scenario_evals.prompt: Restyle the Horizon login screen using Horizon Minimal.
Verify the authenticated shell and a management page at 390x844.
expected: table overflow contained locally when necessary
